conventions_and_corrections: Simple and log returns distinguished; dividends included once; reinvestment assumption for cumulative wealth; portfolio aggregation uses simple returns.
Empirical regularities are not universal laws or predictions. Historical calendars are not current trading schedules.
Uncorrelated does not mean independent. Pointwise iid ACF bounds are not simultaneous confidence bands or proof of independence.
ACF uses the full-series mean and denominator. Box-Pierce/Ljung-Box null, heteroskedasticity and fitted-residual limitations stated.
Sample SD uses n-1; moment kurtosis uses m4/m2^2 with moments divided by n. Normal population kurtosis is 3, excess is 0.
Normal variance-mixture kurtosis derivation assumes a common mean and finite fourth moments. Mixtures alone do not establish temporal clustering.
Intraday variance shares sum to one; interpreting the sum as total return variance requires zero cross-interval covariances.
RV denotes sum of squared intraday log returns; realized volatility is its square root. Decimal squared units and percent squared units differ by 10000.
Open-hours RV excludes overnight variation. Annualization does not restore missing overnight risk.
Realized variance converges to quadratic variation including squared jumps; noise-free continuous variation equals integrated variance.
Independent zero-mean price noise adds expected bias 2N eta^2; one finite path need not produce monotonically ordered estimates.
Ex-post standardization with today's realized volatility is not an ex-ante forecast. Return and volatility measurement windows must match.
Slow ACF alone does not prove true long memory; approximate normality of log volatility is not a universal lognormal law.
